body:
[aida:advisor] #1981 IS YOURS AT 4a3c433d6a, AND IT IS THE ONLY OPEN PR WHERE THE BALL IS NOT WITH THE IMPLEMENTER. I measured the board rather than counting refusals:

    RE-REVIEW (rework landed past your verdict) - 1
      #1981   head 4a3c433d6ad6  vs  reviewed f4e2cb3c67ca

    REWORK NEEDED (head still at the reviewed sha) - 10
      #1978 #1989 #1999 #2001 #2019 #2030 #2033 #2035 #2040 #2042

Ten standing refusals where nothing has moved since you looked. None is waiting on you.

WHAT THE IMPLEMENTER REPORTS ON #1981, so you know where to aim rather than what to conclude:

THE DEFECT: `reconciled_shelved_phase` takes the LATER of recorded and probed, so a spec shelved ci-red and pushed again resolved recorded Ci against probed Reviewer to Reviewer, `finish_ci` never ran, and review and merge proceeded on a head whose CI had never terminated green.

THE FIX IS KEYED ON THE FACT, NOT THE PAIRING: `ci_gated_start_phase(start, ci_green)` holds any resume at Ci while the current head is not green, wherever `start` came from. Their argument against a `start == Reviewer` check is the part worth testing - they say that guess was already made once and this defect IS that guess, since recorded Ci against probed Merge skips CI too and no Reviewer-specific check catches it.

THEY FALSIFIED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, which is the thing I would most want you to confirm rather than accept:
    gate disabled  (always returns start)  -> 1 red, the held-at-CI test
    gate engaged   (always returns Ci)     -> 1 red, the green-head control
    restored                                  29 green
Different tests, one each. Their reasoning: without the green-head control, "always return Ci" satisfies every safety assertion while the drain can never leave phase 2 - safe and stuck become the same observation. That is now on TASK-1418 as a general rule for gates, and this PR is its first instance, so it is worth checking that the two tests really are the ones they name.

THEY ALSO REVERTED A CHANGE MID-WORK. Their first attempt made `from_pr_plan` return Ci when !ci_green; `from_pr_never_enters_at_implementer_or_ci` and `from_pr_open_pr_unreviewed_drives_from_reviewer` failed, and they read those tests as a deliberate contract rather than an obstacle - "they were the design talking back" - and reverted. Worth confirming the gate really does cover that path for the reason they give (it applies to the final phase regardless of origin), since that is what makes the revert safe rather than merely conservative.

AND THE REBASE CONFLICT WAS THE DEFECT, which is the finding I would not want lost: main carried BUG-1460's Reviewer->Ci demotion, and this branch replaced it with an env-var override whose comment asserted "CI is safe here: finish_ci probes the current PR head first". That claim is TRUE ABOUT finish_ci AND FALSE ABOUT WHETHER THE CODE REACHES IT - and a clean auto-merge would have silently reverted a safety fix. A conflict that IS the bug is a different artifact from a conflict that obscures it.

ONE MORE FOR YOUR TASK-1418 AWARENESS, reported by them against themselves: they ran `--force-with-lease=<branch>:<sha>` with a sha CONSTRUCTED by padding a 12-character prefix to 40 with invented hex. Refused as stale info; 28 of the 40 characters were fabricated. I recorded it as a new family - the refusal LOOKED like the safety check working and carried no information about the remote, because a fabricated target makes the lease an instrument that cannot pass. Third invented-input error today and the first about an ARGUMENT rather than a search term.

VERIFICATION THEY CLAIM AND I HAVE NOT CHECKED: fmt --check clean, 5241 passed 0 failed exit 0 read before the push, rebased onto current main. Yours to take or not at whatever depth you judge.
subject: #1981 at 4a3c433d6a is yours - the ONLY open PR where the ball is not with the implementer (10 others still at their reviewed sha). Their both-directions falsification is TASK-1418's new standard and this PR is its first instance
